title: Tech Note: User Configured List Forms
author: Charles “Charlie” Vass, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: 4D v13 selection-based List Box (programmatically built columns)
Per-user list form configuration table (SQL DDL via Begin SQL)

historical_commentary.text: This proof-of-concept builds an end-user-customizable output list form by programmatically constructing List Box columns at runtime and storing each user's configuration as a BLOB in a classic-language table, queried with QUERY/DELETE SELECTION and defined via inline SQL DDL. The core idea of letting end users design their own list views remains a legitimate feature pattern today, but the underlying data access (classic selections, manual QUERY chains) predates ORDA's entity-based, dot-notation approach and the List Box itself predates the object/collection-driven list box model introduced in later 4D versions, both of which now make dynamic column configuration considerably more straightforward.
related_updates: ORDA entity selections and dot-notation queries (4D v16 R5/R6, 2017) are now preferred over classic QUERY/selection-based data access

Object/collection-based list boxes bound to arrays of objects (introduced in later 4D versions) simplify dynamic, user-configurable column layouts compared to manually building selection-based List Box columns
